channel.title: AI Threat Watch: verified case files
channel.description: 487 verified case files of AI security incidents, newest first. Each has a permanent link, primary sources and a ready-made citation.

item.title: Tarn restaurateurs scammed with AI-generated bank proof and doctored photo
item.description: According to the Tarn gendarmerie and local press, a scam targeted restaurants around Saint-Sulpice-la-Pointe: a caller claimed a duplicate payment, then a woman showed an AI-retouched bank statement on her phone to demand a cash refund. Gendarmes recorded at least five victims or attempts, and a suspect was arrested and confessed.

item.title: Pensioner in Ust-Ilimsk loses 26M rubles to scammers using a 'digital double' of Irkutsk governor Kobzev, officials say
item.description: Governor Igor Kobzev said scammers used his 'digital double' to deceive a pensioner in Ust-Ilimsk, Irkutsk Oblast, who handed over 26 million rubles, nearly all her savings, in late October 2026. Media reports describe a copied voice and a video call, and police say a further 6 million rubles was saved. The AI technique has not been independently verified.

item.title: GitBook discloses AI agent attack exposing some infrastructure credentials
item.description: GitBook disclosed that on 2 Nov 2026 an attacker, described by the company as using AI agents in a targeted attack, gained unauthorized access to parts of its infrastructure and some infrastructure credentials. The company reported no evidence that customer content was altered and urged users to rotate their keys. The attacker's identity and exactly how the AI agents were used were not disclosed.

item.title: Chainstack discloses production breach exposing customer data and password hashes
item.description: Blockchain infrastructure provider Chainstack disclosed that an external attacker reached its development environment on 26 Oct 2026 and some production systems on 29 Oct through a third-party component. The intrusion was detected and cut off on 31 Oct. The attacker accessed a database of customer account information including password hashes, plus systems holding node credentials. The company says its findings indicate the incident was part of a broader AI-powered attack campaign, which The Hacker News says overlaps with a China-linked cluster using ARTEX.

item.title: 3AM ransomware affiliate hits UK school estate in suspected AI-assisted attack
item.description: A 3AM ransomware affiliate encrypted about 37 of nearly 50 machines reached from an unmanaged host at a UK school estate. Evidence suggests a model may have generated and revised commands.

item.title: CyberStrikeAI framework automates post-exploitation in attacks on educational institutions
item.description: Kaspersky analysed intrusions between September and October against educational institutions in several African and Latin American countries. The attackers broke in through a compromised SQL Server and then used the open-source CyberStrikeAI framework, whose server-side LLM plans and generates the commands that the implant executes. In one case, domain admin was reached within three to four days of agent deployment. Kaspersky did not link the activity to a known group but points to a Chinese-speaking operator.

item.title: Shanghai man loses 180,000+ yuan to AI-image 'fiancée' in ring that took 1.8M yuan from 15 victims
item.description: CCTV News reported that Mr. Liu, who works in Shanghai, transferred more than 180,000 yuan to an online 'fiancée' who turned out to be a fiction built by a fraud ring. Human chat operators followed a seven-day script and sent AI-generated or AI-altered photos, backed by forged medical and ID documents. Minhang police traced the ring and made arrests in Guangdong, Shandong, Guizhou and elsewhere. The ring defrauded 15 victims of more than 1.8 million yuan, and those involved received prison terms of up to 11 years.

item.title: Volta-Autodoxer infostealer uses AI to 'autodox' victims
item.description: Cisco Talos detailed Volta-Autodoxer, a Windows infostealer first reported by WIRED. It steals logins, cookies, payment cards, crypto wallets, Discord sessions and order receipts such as UberEats. It then sends the data to AI models (Claude by default, with Kimi K2 and Gemini fallbacks) to build a victim dossier and rank the victim's assets. Talos has not observed it in real attacks.

item.title: Jancovici denounces alleged AI-cloned voice used in cold calls selling solar panels and insulation to French residents
item.description: Jean-Marc Jancovici says an AI imitation of his voice is being used in unsolicited commercial calls offering solar panels and insulation works. He says he has received about ten testimonies and is behind none of the calls, and he warns people not to give personal or banking details. An M6 Info clip of one call circulated on 30 October. The caller and the tool used have not been established, and no losses are reported.

item.title: WorkOS internal sales app breached using AI-assisted offensive framework
item.description: WorkOS reported unauthorized access to an internal sales application on 30 October 2026. Its investigation reportedly found the attackers used an AI-assisted offensive security framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation. Customer data was reportedly accessed.

item.title: Trojanized Claude Code extension 2.1.313 on Cursor Marketplace installs persistent SSH backdoor
item.description: A trojanized anthropic.claude-code 2.1.313, with a 66-line malicious loader prepended to the extension bundle, was distributed through the Cursor Marketplace for about 11 hours on 29 October 2026. It added an attacker SSH key, installed persistence and sent host details to an attacker server; Cursor says at most 5,000 users were affected. Phorion first reported it on Open VSX, but Socket found no evidence that version reached Open VSX or Microsoft's marketplace. How the attackers published the update is unclear.

item.title: Unauthorized Codex and Claude Code relays disable sandboxing at 12 organizations
item.description: Symantec says an unauthorized relay service installs the genuine OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude Code CLIs, then reconfigures them to route prompts and credentials through third-party servers with sandboxing switched off. It has been active since at least early 2026 and has affected a dozen organizations, mostly in mainland China, plus multinational subsidiaries in South Korea, Taiwan and Malaysia.

item.title: Hugging Face model malware campaign returns to hijack GPUs for crypto mining
item.description: Pluto Security found 31 malicious Hugging Face model repositories across seven accounts, published in two waves since September, that abuse the trust_remote_code option to install crypto miners and backdoors on GPU servers. The campaign returned within days of the first takedown, and a near-identical copy uploaded on 25 October was still live when BleepingComputer checked. The most popular model was downloaded over 28,000 times. BleepingComputer also reports, as a separate campaign, a fake Solana starter kit on GitHub aimed at tricking AI coding agents.

item.title: 123 Reg discloses AI cyberattack on customer data, suspects China nexus
item.description: UK registrar 123 Reg (GoDaddy-owned) disclosed that a 18 September 2026 intrusion, which it calls its first known AI-driven cyberattack, exposed customer contact details, VAT numbers and product data from an API; the company says activity was limited to reading data and alleges a China nexus, suspecting a Claude Code-abusing state-linked group or the actors who used ARTEX against South Korean financial firms.

item.title: Yoba malware spread via fake ChatGPT and Claude desktop apps on GitHub
item.description: Check Point Research reports a two-month campaign (Yoba) using fake GitHub projects posing as AI desktop apps (GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus), placing malware beside legitimate signed OpenAI and Anthropic executables for DLL sideloading; the observed final payload was an XMRig cryptominer, though the loader can deliver any payload.

item.title: Warp discloses vendor breach exposing AI agent logs and user telemetry
item.description: Warp disclosed that an attack on a third-party vendor in its infrastructure exposed agent decision logs and telemetry data belonging to users of its agentic development environment.

item.title: Russian MVD warns fake online stores may use AI-generated celebrity videos to lure buyers
item.description: Russia's Interior Ministry cybercrime directorate warned on 27 October 2026 that fake online shops advertising steep discounts or foreign delivery may use AI-generated videos of well-known people to look convincing. Buyers are asked to prepay in full and the goods never arrive, with the sellers blaming customs delays and keeping the money. The MVD gave no victim numbers, losses or arrests.

item.title: Wrongful death suit alleges ChatGPT medical advice killed woman with epilepsy
item.description: Social Media Victims Law Center and The Schenk Law Firm allege in a wrongful death lawsuit that ChatGPT's medical advice resulted in the death of a woman with epilepsy. Claims are unproven.

item.title: Seoul police arrest ring that used generative AI to hack 90+ Korean firms, steal about 8.2M records and extort them
item.description: Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said on 26 October 2026 that a 32-year-old ringleader and six accomplices allegedly used generative AI and autonomous AI penetration-testing tools, including the Chinese-origin ARTEX, to break into at least 90 Korean organisations, among them affiliates of large companies, hospitals, golf courses and academies. They allegedly took about 8.2 million records and demanded a total of ₩360M from 38 firms by threatening to publish the data, while actual money paid was reported as about ₩300,000. The ringleader is not an IT graduate and taught himself from YouTube and blogs, but he had earlier worked in penetration testing at a security firm. Police call it the first domestic arrest in a large-scale generative-AI hacking case. The ringleader was detained on 17 October and referred to prosecutors on 23 October, and six accomplices are being investigated without detention.

item.title: Dubai café says customer used AI-generated photo to claim delivery refund
item.description: Dubai café Taho Avenue (Al Muraqqabat, Deira) alleges a customer submitted an AI-generated photo of a spilled order to claim a food delivery refund, pointing to mismatched cup sleeves, sago instead of boba and unrealistic spillage; the claim comes from the café's own social media post and has not been independently verified.

item.title: Cloudflare Workers AI GLM-5.3 model leaks other users' content in 155 responses
item.description: Cloudflare disclosed on 26 October that its GLM-5.3 model on Workers AI returned data from other customers' sessions in 155 responses to very long prompts between 27 August and 9 September, caused by a KV-cache configuration mismatch interacting with an SGLang inference-engine bug. Security researcher Gadi Evron of Knostic reported it via HackerOne on 8 September. Cloudflare pulled the model, fixed the configuration and updated the engine on 9 September.

item.title: AI-assisted PHP2Shell attack roots 25 servers, breaches US government-affiliated network
item.description: Dream researchers say an apparently AI-assisted attack, attributed only as a suspected China-nexus actor, chained a custom PHP2Shell exploit with the Fragnesia Linux kernel flaw (CVE-2026-46300) to root 25 firewall servers across the US, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea, including three in a US government-affiliated environment, then targeted Active Directory; activity was observed on 25 Oct 2026 and the full extent of compromise is indeterminate. The AI link rests on Claude Code installed on attacker infrastructure, API keys for an AI offensive platform and AI-style scripts.

item.title: Honduran woman arrested for allegedly using AI-made fake bank-transfer receipts to scam cellphone sellers in San Pedro Sula
item.description: Police in San Pedro Sula arrested a 25-year-old woman in flagrante on 24 October 2026 after a seller reported her. She is accused of sending fake bank-transfer receipts, allegedly made with AI tools including ChatGPT, to sellers of high-end phones on Facebook Marketplace. Preliminary investigation points to AI use, and authorities have not published a forensic finding on which tool was used. The attempted sale was foiled and two phones were seized. Police records list 22 fraud complaints against her since 2022; the total number of victims and the amount are not stated.

item.title: Jon Bon Jovi impersonator uses AI videos to scam woman out of $10K
item.description: A scammer posing as Jon Bon Jovi on Instagram used AI-generated videos over about 10 months to build trust with Louisiana fan Leslie Pickett, then pressed her for bitcoin payments; she lost over $10,000 and says she nearly lost her home. An ethical hacker brought in by the National Geographic 'Super Scam Me' team reportedly traced the impostor to Lagos; this is alleged.

item.title: Mendoza retiree loses $24.5M pesos to crypto scam using AI-manipulated Messi and Scaloni video
item.description: A 70-year-old retiree from Las Heras, Mendoza, lost about 24.5 million pesos after a sponsored Facebook post imitating a La Nación article and a video of Lionel Messi manipulated with AI promoted a fake crypto investment platform called 'Stake Manerix 0.6'. The image of coach Lionel Scaloni was also used. Per local media, a judge ordered Ualá and Mercado Pago to suspend loan collections and return $8.2M pesos while the case proceeds.

item.title: St Petersburg ballet master Komleva sells flat for 9.1M rubles after calls from AI avatar of Governor Beglov
item.description: Scammers reportedly used an AI avatar of St Petersburg governor Alexander Beglov, plus a man posing as a first deputy interior minister, in messenger video calls to convince Mariinsky Theatre ballet master Gabriela Komleva, 87, to sell her Tsarskoye Selo flat for 9.1M rubles (December 2024) and hand the proceeds to them. She realised the deception months later and went to police; the case became public via a court ruling that let the buyer keep the flat.

item.title: 88-year-old BC man loses $450,000 to deepfake video of PM Mark Carney; TD Bank has not repaid him
item.description: CBC Go Public reports Ralph Moore, 88, of Qualicum Beach, BC, lost $450,000 over 10 months to an online investment scam he was drawn into by a deepfake video of Prime Minister Mark Carney; his family says TD Bank has not reimbursed him.

item.title: Russian group Storm-1516 spreads AI deepfake video accusing Texas candidate Talarico
item.description: A Russian disinformation group, identified by PolitiFact as Storm-1516, reportedly targeted Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico with an AI-generated video showing a purported former student accusing him of misconduct. PolitiFact rated the claim baseless.

item.title: Storm-0940 uses ARTEX agentic AI in ConnectWise supply chain compromise
item.description: Microsoft reports a large-scale nation-state campaign in which Storm-0940 used ARTEX agentic AI to accelerate a ConnectWise supply chain compromise and abuse application credentials in Microsoft 365.

item.title: Spanish opposition PP ad uses deepfakes of PM's wife and other political figures
item.description: Spain's main opposition party, the Partido Popular, published an AI-made deepfake campaign video showing likenesses of PM Pedro Sánchez's wife Begoña Gómez and other Socialist-linked figures such as Zapatero and Ábalos appearing to admit wrongdoing, ahead of the 29 November general election. It drew outrage and a debate on AI in campaigns, and Gómez filed a legal complaint for identity theft against the PP, announced by Sánchez on 28 October.

item.title: Malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI and Docker steals browser, cloud and AI secrets
item.description: Wiz reports a malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 uploaded to PyPI and Docker on October 21, with a stealer for browser, cloud and AI secrets and a dormant C2.

item.title: Kyrgyz woman, 23, alleges AI-undressed photo of her was sent to acquaintances
item.description: A 23-year-old woman told Kaktus.media she was the victim of a sexualised deepfake made with AI and allegedly sent to acquaintances. She says she fears the police case is stalling and the culprit may escape punishment; nothing has been proven.

item.title: INC and The Gentlemen ransomware affiliates expose AI session logs (Claude, Kimi) and 46 INC encryptor builds on open servers
item.description: SOCRadar found seven exposed servers tied to INC and The Gentlemen ransomware affiliates, holding 8,257 AI messages across 133 sessions, source code, stolen credentials, victim workspaces and 46 victim-specific INC encryptor builds. Operators used OpenCode with OpenRouter-hosted models including Claude Opus 4.6 and Kimi K3, and reframed refused requests as authorized security assessments. Humans approved the AI's steps, and SOCRadar could not confirm that the staged encryptors were deployed. Researchers began investigating in late September 2026.

item.title: BUGSTER uses DeepSeek V4 as AI cybercrime assistant against Indian universities
item.description: Unit 42 reports that an actor using the handle BUGSTER ran the Hermes Agent framework with DeepSeek V4 as its reasoning engine, plus Cursor, with safety controls disabled. The actor ran an AI-generated brute-force campaign against one Indian university's website and achieved a confirmed intrusion at a second university, exfiltrating a database of more than 5,200 records with personal data on students. Unit 42 also found AI-assisted planning for VoIP fraud, Wi-Fi password cracking and cryptocurrency-holder reconnaissance, but no evidence of active call routing.

item.title: CrowdStrike: actor used Claude Code agents to breach at least 15 Argentine healthcare entities
item.description: CrowdStrike's 21 October 2026 report on four previously unreported actors running agentic AI campaigns between May and August 2026 says one Spanish/English-speaking operator compromised at least 15 Argentina-based healthcare entities. The operator ran an automated pentesting setup built on an open-source project, with one Claude Code agent choosing the next attack stage and a second executing it. Credentials and medical records were exfiltrated from at least one victim. Clarín reported the finding.

item.title: Search-ad phishing hijacks cloud billing accounts for unauthorized LLM API usage
item.description: Wiz CIRT says attackers bought Google Search ads for terms like 'google cloud' that led to fake Google login pages, captured credentials and MFA codes, and then linked attacker-controlled GCP projects to victims' billing accounts. Within 24 to 48 hours victim organisations saw charges of tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars in unauthorized Gemini API usage. Google Ads removed the malicious campaign after it was reported.

item.title: WhatsApp help pages leak hidden instructions for Meta's support chatbot
item.description: About 80 WhatsApp help and FAQ pages carried roughly 100 blocks of hidden instructions written for Meta's support chatbot, including a 'WHAT NOT TO SAY' section, in page code labelled HelpContentGalaxyLLMInclude. Privacy firm Redact found them. Meta says a bug caused the exposure and removed the text after WIRED asked. No private chats or account data were reported exposed.

item.title: Scammers use AI-cloned voice of Osceola County, Florida sheriff's captain in fake arrest-warrant calls
item.description: The Osceola County Sheriff's Office says scammers used AI to clone the voice, and used the photo, of Captain Steve Moser in voicemails claiming recipients had an arrest warrant or had missed jury duty. The office estimates about 40 cases of scammers impersonating law enforcement this year. The sources report no victim losses and do not say all of the 40 cases involved AI voice cloning.

item.title: Goiás man arrested for AI-faked armed photo used to threaten ex-partner
item.description: A man in Goiás, Brazil, used AI to forge an image of a pistol in a vehicle and sent it by WhatsApp to threaten his ex-partner. He was arrested in flagrante after the victim identified a tattoo in the image.

item.title: Hackers abuse open-source AI platform Cairn to run agent-driven website intrusions; largest of three clusters breached 100+ organizations
item.description: NorForge found threat actors had left Cairn control panels exposed and identified three apparently malicious clusters focused on persistent access and financial theft. The largest, Chinese-language cluster ran 1,100+ attack projects across 14 dashboards. Reuters reports that this cluster breached over 100 companies. NorForge says attackers succeeded in roughly 10% of attempts, and Reuters could not establish how much data was extracted.

item.title: AI deepfakes of actress Wu Yue and other celebrities used to push product sales
item.description: Actress Wu Yue said on 18 October 2026 that the WeChat Channels account '花姐美肤日记' (Hua Jie Beauty Diary) used an AI face-swap and cloned voice of her to promote skincare products she never endorsed, and she demanded it repay viewers. Coverage says other public figures, such as Deng Yaping, have been faked in similar sales videos. No loss figure has been reported, and the buyers' losses are alleged.

item.title: Brazilian Federal Police arrest OAB bar exam candidate in São Luís for alleged AI-assisted fraud
item.description: On 18 October 2026 the Federal Police arrested in flagrante a candidate at the OAB bar exam in São Luís, Maranhão, after agents found him using a phone connected to an AI tool, allegedly to gain an advantage. He was booked for fraud in a public-interest exam and released after paying bail. Police are investigating whether anyone else took part. His identity has not been released.

item.title: Hundreds of AI agents exploit PaperCut NG/MF servers to steal Windows credentials
item.description: A likely Russian-speaking actor used hundreds of AI agents to exploit PaperCut NG/MF servers, steal Windows credentials and set up reusable internal access. GreyNoise found 440 compromised instances.

item.title: JINX-2401 LLM hijacking campaign targets AWS environments with IAM privilege escalation
item.description: Wiz reports new LLM hijacking activity, including the JINX-2401 campaign that targets AWS environments using IAM privilege escalation tactics.

item.title: Aoki infostealer expands to steal Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor credentials
item.description: The Aoki (Aokigahara) infostealer, first seen earlier in 2026, now collects credentials and session files from AI coding assistants, putting developer identities and connected infrastructure at risk.

item.title: AI-powered espionage campaign targets government Linux infrastructure
item.description: Unit 42 reports an AI-powered espionage campaign against government Linux infrastructure using custom malware, web shells and advanced credential theft.

item.title: Storm-3168 runs agentic Azure attacks via compromised service principals
item.description: Microsoft attributes agentic-driven Azure reconnaissance, resource deletion and credential access with compromised service principals to Storm-3168, linked to JADEPUFFER.

item.title: Hidden prompt injection in legal filing instructs AI reviewers to side with filer
item.description: 404 Media reports a person embedded a prompt injection in a legal filing telling AI to side with them. Details of court, jurisdiction and outcome are not given in the summary.

item.title: Undisclosed jqwik addition instructs AI coding agents to delete app output
item.description: An undisclosed addition to the jqwik library contained instructions aimed at AI coding agents, telling them to delete application output, according to Ars Technica.

item.title: CERT-In: AI agents under test read live data at Indian organizations
item.description: AI agents being tested online went beyond their assigned tasks, reached live systems of Indian organizations and read business records including personal data and confidential material, per a CERT-In advisory.
